RUNBOOK: Release Rollback / Production Core
Service owner: Engineering response. Revision 1; approved for active operations.

Preconditions / step 1
Operators confirm preconditions in the service dashboard and record the action in the change log. Any exception remains bounded by the scope and approval recorded with the case.

Preconditions / step 2
An earlier broad exception is retired for production core; only a separately approved exception remains applicable.

Preconditions / step 3
Questions about ownership go to the Engineering lead. The lead can request specialist review when the facts do not fit the ordinary pattern.

Preconditions / step 4
This material also appears in related guidance for neighboring groups. Those references are useful context but do not override the current production core record.

Steps / step 5
For audit purposes, the decision trail should show who checked scope, who approved the action, and what evidence was available at the time.

Steps / step 6
The team should explain the applicable condition in plain language to the requester. It should preserve the approval reference alongside the outcome.

Steps / step 7
Historical notes explain why the current rule changed, but they are not themselves the operative requirement for a new request.

Steps / step 8
The approved schedule is reviewed when responsibilities or operating conditions change. Until a replacement is published, teams continue to use the effective record.

Rollback / step 9
The deployment recovery workflow should avoid copying a decision from another tenant. Each organization maintains its own approval and evidence history.

Rollback / step 10
During routine review, the owner compares recent cases for release rollback with the approved wording and corrects any outdated local summaries.

Rollback / step 11
The deployment recovery record is the normal place to attach supporting evidence. Its owner checks that the relevant approval chain was followed before the case is finalized.

Rollback / step 12
Operators confirm preconditions in the service dashboard and record the action in the change log. The record of that review should name the responsible team and the date of the decision.

Escalation / step 13
Recorded dates establish when this guidance was in force. A later draft is not effective merely because its timestamp is newer.

Escalation / step 14
When operations hand off a case, the next team checks the source record rather than relying solely on a brief chat or an earlier ticket.

Escalation / step 15
Applicability is limited to production core; a neighboring scope can have a different approved value. Teams must verify the requester and location before acting on release rollback.

Escalation / step 16
For production core, the standard rule governing release rollback sets the decision window at 36 minutes. This figure applies to deployment recovery after the responsible owner confirms the scope. A separate approved exception may change the result for a qualifying case. A broad exception may be applied without individual approval.

Previously, a broad exception was available without separate approval.
